facts.statement: Kentrosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period, specifically from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian ages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian to Tithonian),

facts.statement: The genus Kentrosaurus was described by the German paleontologist Edwin Hennig in 1915.
facts.quote: authority: Hennig, 1915

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus has two junior objective synonyms: Kentrurosaurus and Doryphorosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Kentrurosaurus Hennig, 1916 Doryphorosaurus Nopcsa, 1916

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus is a genus of stegosaurid dinosaur found in the Lindi Region of Tanzania.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus ( ; ) is a genus of stegosaurid dinosaur from the Late Jurassic in Lindi Region of Tanzania.

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analyses suggest Kentrosaurus is a derived member of Stegosauria and a close relative of Stegosaurus within the family Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: Often thought to be a "primitive" member of the Stegosauria, several recent cladistic analyses find it as more derived than many other stegosaurs, and a close relative of Stegosaurus from the North American Morrison Formation within the Stegosauridae.

facts.statement: Fossils of the type species K. aethiopicus are found only in the Tendaguru Formation, dating to about 152 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossils of K. aethiopicus have been found only in the Tendaguru Formation, dated to the late Kimmeridgian and early Tithonian ages, about 152 million years ago.

facts.statement: Hundreds of Kentrosaurus bones were unearthed by German expeditions in German East Africa between 1909 and 1912.
facts.quote: Hundreds of bones were unearthed by German expeditions to German East Africa between 1909 and 1912.

facts.statement: Adult Kentrosaurus measured approximately 4 to 4.5 meters in length and weighed between 700 and 1600 kilograms.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus generally measured around 4 - 4.5 m in length as an adult, and weighed about 700 - 1600 kg.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus was a quadruped that walked on all fours with straight hindlimbs.
facts.quote: It walked on all fours with straight hindlimbs.

facts.statement: The plates on Kentrosaurus gradually merged into spikes located on its hips and tail.
facts.quote: These plates gradually merged into spikes on the hip and tail.

facts.statement: The longest spikes on Kentrosaurus were located at the tail end and were used for active defense.
facts.quote: The longest spikes were on the tail end and were used to actively defend the animal.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus possessed a long spike on each shoulder.
facts.quote: There also was a long spike on each shoulder.

facts.statement: Two different types of thigh bones in Kentrosaurus suggest sexual dimorphism, with one sex being larger and stouter than the other.
facts.quote: The thigh bones come in two different types, suggesting that one sex was larger and more stout than the other.

facts.statement: The first Kentrosaurus fossils were discovered in 1909, identified as a stegosaur by Werner Janensch in 1910, and formally described by Edwin Hennig in 1915.
facts.quote: The first fossils of Kentrosaurus were discovered by the German Tendaguru Expedition in 1909, recognised as belonging to a stegosaur by expedition leader Werner Janensch on 24 July 1910, and described by German palaeontologist Edwin Hennig in 1915.

facts.statement: The name Kentrosaurus was coined by Hennig from Greek words meaning "sharp point" and "lizard".
facts.quote: The name Kentrosaurus was coined by Hennig and comes from the Greek /κέντρον, meaning "sharp point" or "prickle", and /σαῦρος meaning "lizard",

facts.statement: Hennig named the species aethiopicus to indicate the animal's African origin.
facts.quote: Hennig added the specific name aethiopicus to denote the provenance from Africa.

facts.statement: A naming controversy arose shortly after description because the name Kentrosaurus was very similar to the ceratopsian Centrosaurus.
facts.quote: Soon after its description, a controversy arose over the stegosaur's name, which is very similar to the ceratopsian Centrosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1916, Hennig renamed the stegosaur Kentrurosaurus and Nopcsa renamed the genus Doryphorosaurus to avoid homonymy with Centrosaurus.
facts.quote: Hennig renamed his stegosaur Kentrurosaurus, "pointed-tail lizard", in 1916, while Hungarian paleontologist Franz Nopcsa renamed the genus Doryphorosaurus, "lance-bearing lizard", the same year.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus remains were found in four quarries in the Middle Saurian Beds and one quarry in the Upper Saurian Beds.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus remains were uncovered in four quarries in the Mittlere Saurierschichten (Middle Saurian Beds) and one quarry in the Obere Saurierschichten (Upper Saurian Beds).

facts.statement: The German Expedition found over 1200 bones belonging to about fifty individuals, though many were destroyed during World War II.
facts.quote: During four field seasons, the German Expedition found over 1200 bones of Kentrosaurus, belonging to about fifty individuals, many of which were destroyed during the Second World War.

facts.statement: Almost all remaining Kentrosaurus material is housed in the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin, containing roughly 350 specimens.
facts.quote: Today, almost all remaining material is housed in the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin (roughly 350 remaining specimens),

facts.statement: Cranial material previously thought lost during World War II was later found in a basement cupboard.
facts.quote: However, all the supposedly lost cranial material was later found in a drawer of a basement cupboard.

facts.statement: Hennig designated a lectotype in 1925 consisting of the most complete partial skeleton, inventorised as MB.R.4800.1 through MB.R.4800.37.
facts.quote: In the original description, Hennig did not designate a holotype specimen. However, in a detailed monography on the osteology, systematic position and palaeobiology of Kentrosaurus in 1925, Hennig picked the most complete partial skeleton, today inventorised as MB.R.4800.1 through MB.R.4800.37, as a lectotype (see syntype).

facts.statement: The type locality for Kentrosaurus is Kindope, Tanzania, located north of Tendaguru hill.
facts.quote: The type locality is Kindope, Tanzania, north of Tendaguru hill.

facts.statement: Heinrich Mallison clarified in 2011 that MB.R.4800 is the correct lectotype and that other material discovered before 1912 are paralectotypes.
facts.quote: In 2011, Heinrich Mallison clarified that all the material known to Hennig in 1915, i.e. all the bones discovered before 1912, when Hermann Heck concluded the last German excavations, are paralectotypes, and that MB.R.4800 is the correct lectotype.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus is classified as a small stegosaur.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus was a small stegosaur.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a typical dinosaur body plan featuring a small head, long neck, short forelimbs, long hindlimbs, and a long, horizontal, muscular tail.
facts.quote: It had the typical dinosaurian body bauplan, characterised by a small head, a long neck, short forelimbs and long hindlimbs, and a long, horizontal and muscular tail.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus exhibited typical stegosaurid traits including an elongated, flat head, powerful forelimbs, erect hindlimbs, and plates and spikes along its back.
facts.quote: Typical stegosaurid traits included the elongation and flatness of the head, the powerful build of the forelimbs, erect and pillar-like hindlimbs and an array of plates and spikes running along both sides of the top mid-line of the animal.

facts.statement: Some specimens suggest that relatively larger individuals of Kentrosaurus could have existed.
facts.quote: Some specimens suggest that relatively larger individuals could have existed.

facts.statement: The long tail of Kentrosaurus placed its center of mass unusually far back for a quadrupedal animal.
facts.quote: The long tail of Kentrosaurus results in a position of the center of mass that is unusually far back for a quadrupedal animal.

facts.statement: The straight femora of Kentrosaurus indicate a straight and vertical limb position, unlike typical bipeds.
facts.quote: However, the femora are straight in Kentrosaurus, as opposed to typical bipeds, indicating a straight and vertical limb position.

facts.statement: In Kentrosaurus, the robust forelimbs supported 10 to 15% of the bodyweight, assisting the hindlimbs which were powered by massive thigh muscles.
facts.quote: The hindlimbs, though powered by massive thigh muscles attached to a long ilium, did not support the animal alone, and the very robust forelimbs took up 10 to 15% of the bodyweight.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Kentrosaurus is a primitive or derived member of Stegosauria, with recent analyses suggesting it is more derived and closely related to Stegosaurus.
facts.quote: Often thought to be a "primitive" member of the Stegosauria, several recent cladistic analyses find it as more derived than many other stegosaurs, and a close relative of Stegosaurus from the North American Morrison Formation within the Stegosauridae.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a long, narrow skull that was small relative to its body size.
facts.quote: The long and narrow skull was small in proportion to the body.

facts.statement: A beak extending along much of the jaws likely prevented the presence of cheeks in Kentrosaurus.
facts.quote: The presence of a beak extended along much of the jaws may have precluded the presence of cheeks in stegosaurs.

facts.statement: Some researchers debate whether ridges on Kentrosaurus supported fleshy cheeks instead of a beak.
facts.quote: Other researchers have interpreted these ridges as modified versions of similar structures in other ornithischians which might have supported fleshy cheeks, rather than beaks.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Kentrosaurus had 13 preserved tooth sockets on its inner side.
facts.quote: The dentary has 13 preserved alveoli on the dorsomedial side and they are slightly convex in lateral and dorsal views.

facts.statement: Wear patterns on Kentrosaurus teeth indicate that it ground its food.
facts.quote: Wear facets show that they did grind their food.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a neck made of 13 vertebrae, with the first fused to the skull and the second following it.
facts.quote: The neck was composed of 13 cervical (neck) vertebrae, the first being the atlas which was strongly fused to the occipital region of the skull and followed by the axis.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus possessed 13 tall back vertebrae with short central bodies.
facts.quote: The dorsal column consists of 13 dorsal (back) vertebrae which are tall and have short centra.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a sacrum made of 6 fused vertebrae forming a solid plate.
facts.quote: The sacrum (part of pelvis with vertebrae) consists of 6 fused centra, the first being a loose sacrodorsal, while the rest of the centra's transverse processes (extensions of bone) are fused to the dorsal parts of the sacral ribs into a solid sacral plate.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a unique ilium where the front blade widened laterally instead of tapering like in other stegosaurs.
facts.quote: The ilium is notable in that the preacetabular process, front blade, of the ilium widens laterally, to the front outer side, and does not taper unlike in all other stegosaurs.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had 29 tail vertebrae, with 27 to 29 fused together to attach the tail spikes.
facts.quote: The caudal (tail) vertebrae are 29 in number, though 27-29 are coossified for attachment to the thagomizers (tail spikes).

facts.statement: The chevron bones under Kentrosaurus tail vertebrae were shaped like an inverted T.
facts.quote: The chevrons, bones pointing to below from the bottom side of the tail vertebrae, have the shape of an inverted T.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had much shorter forelimbs than its stocky hindlimbs, creating an unusual posture.
facts.quote: The fore limbs were much shorter than the stocky hind limbs, which resulted in an unusual posture.

facts.statement: The largest known femur of Kentrosaurus measured 665 mm and was the longest bone in its body.
facts.quote: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest element in the body, with the largest known femur measuring 665 mm from the proximal to distal end.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus feet ended in three toes, each tipped with a hoof-like claw.
facts.quote: The pes (foot) terminated in 3 toes, all of which had hoof-like unguals (claws).

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus was covered in extensive bony armor consisting of small plates and spikes of various shapes.
facts.quote: Typically for a stegosaur, Kentrosaurus had extensive osteoderm (bony structures in the skin) covering, including small plates (probably located on the neck and anterior trunk), and spikes of various shapes.

facts.statement: One specimen of Kentrosaurus had a spike with a bone core length of 731 millimeters.
facts.quote: The spikes of Kentrosaurus are very elongated, with one specimen having a bone core length of 731 millimetres.

facts.statement: Researchers believe the spikes and plates of Kentrosaurus were likely covered by a layer of horn.
facts.quote: The spikes and plates were likely covered by horn.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows a pair of closely spaced spikes articulated with the tail tip and other spikes regularly spaced in pairs along the tail.
facts.quote: A pair of closely spaced spikes was found articulated with a tail tip, and a number of spikes were found apparently regularly spaced in pairs along the path of an articulated tail.

facts.statement: One type of Kentrosaurus spike is strongly asymmetrical with a very broad base, differing from all others.
facts.quote: There is one type of spike that differs from all others in being strongly, and not only slightly, asymmetrical, and having a very broad base.

facts.statement: While classic reconstructions placed a unique broad-based spike on the hips, recent reconstructions based on Chinese stegosaurs place it on the shoulder.
facts.quote: Because of bone morphology classic reconstructions placed it on the hips, at the iliac blade, while many recent reconstructions place it on the shoulder, because a similarly shaped spike is known to have existed on the shoulder in the Chinese stegosaurs Gigantspinosaurus and Huayangosaurus.

facts.statement: The only accepted species of Kentrosaurus is Kentrosaurus aethiopicus, named by Hennig in 1915.
facts.quote: The type and sole accepted species of Kentrosaurus is Kentrosaurus aethiopicus, named by Hennig in 1915.

facts.statement: Hennig assigned Kentrosaurus to the family Stegosauridae in 1915 based on dermal armor and angled neural spines on the tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: In Hennig's 1915 description, Kentrosaurus was assigned to the family Stegosauridae due to the preservation of dermal armor and features like posterodorsally angled neural spines on the caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: A 2025 phylogenetic analysis recovered Kentrosaurus as a member of the subfamily Dacentrurinae.
facts.quote: In 2025, phylogenetic analysis conducted by Sánchez-Fenollosa & Cobos recovered Kentrosaurus as a member of Dacentrurinae.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus was a herbivore that swallowed large chunks of fodder with little chewing.
facts.quote: Like all ornithischians, Kentrosaurus was a herbivore. The fodder was barely chewed and swallowed in large chunks.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus could feed at heights of up to 1.7 meters while on all fours.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus was capable of eating at heights of up to 1.7 m when on all fours.

facts.statement: By rearing up on its hind legs, Kentrosaurus could potentially feed at heights of 3.3 meters.
facts.quote: In this pose, Kentrosaurus could have fed at heights of 3.3 m.

facts.statement: The ratio of robust to gracile femurs was 2:1, suggesting that the more common robust form likely represented females.
facts.quote: The occurrence ratio of the robust morph to the gracile one was 2:1, and it is likely that the higher percentage of animals were females.

facts.statement: Based on femur ratios, it is assumed that Kentrosaurus males may have mated with multiple females, a behavior seen in other vertebrates.
facts.quote: Because of this ratio, it was considered reasonable to assume that in their society, Kentrosaurus males mated with more than one female, a behaviour also found in other vertebrates.

facts.statement: Due to armor obstacles, researchers hypothesize Kentrosaurus pairs may have mated back-to-back with the female in a lordosis posture.
facts.quote: As the plates and spikes would have been obstacles during copulation, it is possible that pairs mated back-to-back with the female staying still in a lordosis posture as the male maneuvers his penis into her cloaca.

facts.statement: A 2013 study concluded Kentrosaurus had a higher growth rate than Stegosaurus and Scutellosaurus based on rapid deposition of vascularized bone.
facts.quote: In 2013, a study by Ragna Redelstorff e.a. concluded that the bone histology of Kentrosaurus indicated that it had a higher growth rate than reported for Stegosaurus and Scutellosaurus, in view of the relatively rapid deposition of highly vascularised fibrolamellar bone.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a highly mobile tail containing at least forty vertebrae.
facts.quote: Because the tail had at least forty caudal vertebrae, it was highly mobile.

facts.statement: The tail of Kentrosaurus could swing at speeds of up to 50 km/h.
facts.quote: Swing speeds at the tail end may have been as high as 50 km/h.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus likely used its tail spikes to slash attackers or stab soft tissues and break ribs or facial bones.
facts.quote: Continuous rapid swings would have allowed the spikes to slash open the skin of its attacker or to stab the soft tissues and break the ribs or facial bones.

facts.statement: Earlier researchers suggested Kentrosaurus might have defended itself by charging rearward through attackers like a porcupine.
facts.quote: Earlier interpretations of the defensive behaviour of Kentrosaurus included the suggestion that the animal might have charged to the rear, to run through attackers with its spines, in the way of modern porcupines.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that Kentrosaurus adopted a sprawling posture when defending itself.
facts.quote: It is hypothesised that the animal adopted a sprawling posture when defending itself.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had thinner spikes than Stegosaurus, making them more prone to bending.
facts.quote: Compared to the more robust spikes of Stegosaurus, the thinner spikes of Kentrosaurus were at greater risk of bending.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus lived in what is now Tanzania during the Late Jurassic in the Tendaguru Formation.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus lived in what is now Tanzania in the Late Jurassic Tendaguru Formation.

facts.statement: The main Kentrosaurus fossils were found in the Middle Saurian Beds dating to the upper Kimmeridgian.
facts.quote: The main Kentrosaurus quarries were located in the Middle Saurian Beds dating from the upper Kimmeridgian.

facts.statement: The boundary between the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages is dated to 152.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Since 2012, the boundary between the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian is dated at 152.1 million year ago.

facts.statement: The genus Kentrosaurus was named by Edwin Hennig in 1915.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Edwin Hennig, 1915

facts.statement: The species K. aethiopicus was named by Hennig in 1915.
facts.quote: species_authority: Hennig, 1915

facts.statement: Hundreds of bones were unearthed by German expeditions in East Africa between 1909 and 1912.
facts.quote: Cientos de huesos fueron desenterrados por las expediciones alemanas al África oriental alemana entre 1909 y 1912.

facts.statement: Although no complete skeletons are known, the remains provided an almost complete picture of the animal's construction.
facts.quote: Aunque no se conocen esqueletos completos, los restos proporcionaron una imagen casi completa de la construcción del animal.

facts.statement: Adult Kentrosaurus generally measured around 4.5 meters in length and weighed approximately 1.1 tons.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus generalmente medía alrededor de 4,5 metros de longitud como adulto, y pesaba aproximadamente una 1,1 toneladas.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a row, likely double, of small plates running down its neck and back.
facts.quote: Tenía una fila, probablemente doble, de platos pequeños que le bajaban por el cuello y la espalda.

facts.statement: The longest spikes were located at the tail end, which were used for active defense.
facts.quote: Los picos más largos estaban en el extremo de la cola, los cuales usaban para defenderse activamente.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus also had a long spine on each shoulder.
facts.quote: También había una espina larga en cada hombro.

facts.statement: The femur bones come in two different types, suggesting one sex was larger and more robust than the other.
facts.quote: Los huesos del muslo vienen en dos tipos diferentes, lo que sugiere que un sexo era más grande y más robusto que el otro.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus was a small stegosaurian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Kentrosaurus era un pequeño estegosáurido.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a typical body plan with a small head, long neck, short forelimbs, long hindlimbs, and a long, horizontal, muscular tail.
facts.quote: Tenía el típico plan corporal de estos dinosaurios, caracterizado por una cabeza pequeña, un cuello largo, extremidades anteriores cortas y extremidades posteriores largas, y una cola larga, horizontal y musculosa.

facts.statement: A reconstructed skeleton of Kentrosaurus measures 4.5 meters in total length from snout to tail tip.
facts.quote: La longitud total de una montura esquelética compuesta en el Museum für Naturkunde de Berlín, Alemania, desde la punta del hocico hasta la punta de la cola es de 4,5 metros.

facts.statement: Individual fossil elements suggest Kentrosaurus could have reached a total length of 5.5 meters.
facts.quote: Se encontraron elementos individuales más grandes, de modo que el animal probablemente podría alcanzar una longitud total de 5,5 metros.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated a 4-meter-long Kentrosaurus weighed 700 kilograms.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimó el peso de un Kentrosaurus de 4 metros de largo, en 700 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had an unusually rearward center of mass for a quadruped due to its long tail.
facts.quote: La larga cola del Kentrosaurus da como resultado una posición del centro de masa que está inusualmente muy atrás para un animal cuadrúpedo.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus possessed straight femurs indicating a vertical limb posture, unlike typical bipeds.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los fémures son rectos en Kentrosaurus, a diferencia de los bípedos típicos, lo que indica una posición de extremidad recta y vertical.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus relied on its robust forelimbs to support 10 to 15% of its body weight, as its hind limbs alone could not support the animal.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, las extremidades posteriores, aunque alimentadas por enormes músculos del muslo unidos a un ilion largo, no soportaban al animal solo, y las extremidades anteriores muy robustas ocupaban del 10 al 15% del peso corporal.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus is notable for having neural spines on its tail that do not run subparallel like in most dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Lo más notable es que las espinas neurales, las extensiones superiores de las vértebras en forma de cuchilla, en la cola no corren subparalelas, como en la mayoría de los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus tail spines pointed backward in the front third, were nearly vertical in the middle third, and curved forward obliquely at the rear.
facts.quote: En el tercio delantero de la cola, apuntan hacia atrás, en la dirección habitual. Sin embargo, en la cola media, son casi verticales, y más atrás tienen forma de gancho y apuntan oblicuamente hacia adelante.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus dorsal vertebrae had neural arches more than twice the height of the vertebral body, filled with an extremely spacious neural canal.
facts.quote: También es típico que las vértebras dorsales tengan un arco neural más del doble de alto que el centro, el cuerpo vertebral, y casi completamente ocupado por el canal neural extremadamente espacioso.

facts.statement: The preacetabular process of Kentrosaurus's ilium widened laterally toward the front-outer side instead of narrowing.
facts.quote: El proceso preacetabular, la lámina frontal del ilion se ensancha lateralmente, hacia el lado externo frontal, y no se estrecha.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had transverse processes extending along its tail up to the twenty-eighth vertebra.
facts.quote: Los procesos transversales, las extensiones laterales, de la cola están presentes hasta la vigésima octava vértebra de la serie.

facts.statement: Frontal tail vertebrae in Kentrosaurus had rod-shaped transverse processes with narrow bases that did not touch the fused sacral plate.
facts.quote: Los procesos transversales de las vértebras de la cola frontal tienen forma de varilla con bases estrechas y no tocan la placa formada por la fusión de los procesos de las vértebras sacras.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had inverted T-shaped chevrons pointing downward from the underside of its tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Los galones, huesos que apuntan hacia abajo desde el lado inferior de las vértebras de la cola, tienen la forma de una T invertida.

facts.statement: In Kentrosaurus, the ilium was equal to or longer than the femur.
facts.quote: La longitud del ilion es igual o mayor que la del fémur.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus was covered in osteoderms including small plates likely on the neck and anterior trunk, and spines of various shapes.
facts.quote: Como es típico para un estegosáurido, Kentrosaurus tenía una amplia cobertura de osteodermos, estructuras óseas en la piel, que incluía pequeñas placas, probablemente ubicadas en el cuello y el tronco anterior y espinas de varias formas.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus spines were very long, with one specimen having a bone core length of 731 millimeters.
facts.quote: Las espinas de Kentrosaurus son muy alargadas, con un espécimen que tiene una longitud del núcleo óseo de 731 milímetros.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus plates had a thickened middle section, resembling modified spines.
facts.quote: Las placas tienen una sección engrosada en el medio, como si fueran espinas modificadas.

facts.statement: Hennig and Janensch identified 15 pairs of dermal armor elements in Kentrosaurus that gradually changed from short flat plates in the front to long pointed spines in the rear.
facts.quote: Hennig y Janensch, al agrupar los elementos de la armadura dérmica en cuatro tipos distintos, reconocieron un cambio aparentemente continuo de forma entre ellos, placas más cortas y más planas en la parte delantera fusionándose gradualmente en espinas más largas y puntiagudas hacia la parte posterior, sugiriendo una distribución ininterrumpida a lo largo de todo el cuerpo, en 15 pares.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus likely had two rows of osteoderms along its back, contrasting with North American Stegosaurus which had one row of plates and two rows of spikes.
facts.quote: Debido a que cada tipo de osteodermos se encontró en versiones reflejadas izquierda y derecha, parece probable que todos los tipos de osteodermos se distribuyeron en dos filas a lo largo de la parte posterior del animal, un marcado contraste con el mejor conocido Stegosaurus de América del Norte, que tenía una hilera de placas en el cuello, el tronco y la cola, y dos hileras de púas en la punta de la cola.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus had a unique robust spine that was slightly asymmetric with a very wide base.
facts.quote: Hay un tipo de espina que difiere de todas las demás por su robustez, es ligeramente asimétrica y por tener una base muy amplia.

facts.statement: Recent reconstructions place a unique Kentrosaurus spine on the shoulder based on similar shoulder spines found in Chinese stegosaurs Gigantspinosaurus and Huayangosaurus.
facts.quote: Debido a la morfología ósea, las reconstrucciones clásicas la colocaron en las caderas, en la lámina ilíaca, mientras que muchas reconstrucciones recientes la colocan en el hombro, porque se sabe que existió una espina de forma similar en el hombro en los estegosáuridos chinos Gigantspinosaurus y Huayangosaurus.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus fossils were first discovered by the German Tendaguru Expedition in 1909, identified as a stegosaur by Werner Janensch on July 24, 1910, and described by Edwin Hennig in 1915.
facts.quote: Los primeros fósiles de Kentrosaurus fueron descubiertos por la Expedición Tendaguru alemana en 1909, reconocida como perteneciente a un estegosáurido por el líder de la expedición Werner Janensch el 24 de julio de 1910 y descrita por el paleontólogo alemán Edwin Hennig en 1915.

facts.statement: The name Kentrosaurus comes from Greek words meaning "sharp point" and "lizard," with the specific name aethiopicus indicating its African origin.
facts.quote: El nombre Kentrosaurus fue acuñado por Hennig y proviene del griego kentron, κέντρον, que significa "punta afilada" o "pinchazo", y sauros, σαῦρος que significa "lagarto", Hennig agregó el nombre específico aethiopicus para denotar la procedencia de África.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus fossils were found in four quarries in the Middle Saurian Beds and one quarry in the Upper Saurian Beds.
facts.quote: A partir de 1909, los restos de Kentrosaurus fueron descubiertos en cuatro canteras en Mittlere Saurierschichten, los Lechos Saurios Medios y una cantera en Obere Saurierschichten, los Lechos Saurianos Superiores.

facts.statement: The German expedition found over 1200 Kentrosaurus bones belonging to about fifty individuals during four field seasons, many destroyed in World War II.
facts.quote: Durante cuatro temporadas de campo, la expedición alemana encontró más de 1200 huesos de Kentrosaurus, pertenecientes a unos cincuenta individuos, muchos de los cuales fueron destruidos durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial.

facts.statement: Today, nearly all remaining Kentrosaurus material is in the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin with about 350 specimens, while the University of Tübingen holds a composite mount with about 50% original bones.
facts.quote: Hoy, casi todo el material restante se encuentra en el Museum für Naturkunde Berlin, aproximadamente 350 especímenes restantes, mientras que el museo del Instituto de Geociencias de la Universidad de Tübingen alberga una montura compuesta, aproximadamente el 50% de los cuales son huesos originales.

facts.statement: The Kentrosaurus mount was dismantled during a 2006-2007 museum renovation and remounted in an improved pose by Research Casting International.
facts.quote: El montaje fue desmantelado durante la renovación del museo entre 2006 y 2007 y lo volvió a montar en una pose mejorada por Research Casting International.

facts.statement: All supposedly lost cranial material was later found in a cabinet in the basement.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, todo el material craneal supuestamente perdido se encontró más tarde en un cajón de un armario del sótano.

facts.statement: In 1993, fragmentary Wyoming fossils named Stegosaurus longispinus by Charles Gilmore in 1914 were classified as a North American species of Kentrosaurus, K. longispinus.
facts.quote: El material fósil fragmentario de Wyoming, llamado Stegosaurus longispinus por Charles Gilmore en 1914, fue clasificado en 1993 como una especie norteamericana de Kentrosaurus, como K . longispinus.

facts.statement: The classification of S. longispinus as K. longispinus was not accepted by the paleontological community, and it is now assigned to its own genus, Alcovasaurus, which differs in having longer tail spikes and different pelvic and vertebral structures.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, esta acción no fue aceptada por la comunidad paleontológica, y S. longispinus ha sido asignado a su propio género, Alcovasaurus, que difiere de Kentrosaurus en tener puntas de cola más alargadas y la estructura de la pelvis y las vértebras.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus lived between 161.5 and 143.1 million years ago during the Oxfordian to Tithonian stages.

facts.statement: Kentrosaurus was a herbivore, like all ornithischian dinosaurs.

facts.statement: When on all fours, Kentrosaurus could reach vegetation up to 1.7 meters high.

facts.statement: A 2013 study concluded that Kentrosaurus had a higher growth rate than Stegosaurus based on bone histology.
